findings.message: This diff grants `delivery:proposal:sync@assigned` to Engineer and `@managed` to PM so they can use sync_specclaw. The same permission also opens the existing `sync_proposal` MCP tool (mcp.ts:76). That tool calls syncProposal directly and skips every 062 guard: it accepts `phase: "released"`, it can move a proposal back a phase, it never checks the linked repo or staleness, and it can rekey hand-made proposals. Before this change only Admin and service principals held this permission. Fix: give the push its own permission (e.g. `delivery:proposal:push`) and grant that one instead. Or put the 062 guards (no Released, no step back) inside syncProposal so that every caller gets them.
findings.scenario: An Engineer on CON calls sync_proposal {projectKey:"CON", key:"CON-014", phase:"released", …}. The proposal becomes Released with no Prod deployment, which breaks 'Released belongs to Prod deployments'.

findings.message: The retention entry for delivery.sync_push uses `action: "anonymise"`, and core/privacy/apply.ts runs that rule as an UPDATE. amax_app gets only `select, insert, delete` on the table. Erasure, and later the daily purge, then fail with 'permission denied', so a person who pushed can't be erased (032, a legal duty). Fix: add `update` to the grant, as delivery.task and delivery.commit_time have.
findings.scenario: An erasure request for Kasun (who has sync_push rows) is approved and completed. eraseRule runs `update delivery.sync_push …` and gets a permission error, so the erasure can't complete.

findings.message: `repoUrl` is the raw output of `git remote get-url origin`. For HTTPS remotes this often holds a credential (`https://x-access-token:ghp_…@github.com/…`). The plugin sends it to amax, and the MCP server writes every call's args into the append-only `core.trace_event` (packages/mcp/src/server.ts:41), so the token is stored for good. normaliseRepo strips the userinfo only after the trace is written. Fix: strip the userinfo in the reader before sending, e.g. send `normaliseRepo(url)`, and regenerate the bundle.
findings.scenario: origin is https://x-access-token:ghp_abc@github.com/example/portal.git, and /amax:sync-specclaw runs. ghp_abc is written to core.trace_event, which can't be deleted.

findings.message: The stale check trusts the client's `committedAt` and sets no upper bound on it. Once a push with a future date is applied, every later real push on that branch reads as stale until that date passes. The commit date can come from a skewed machine clock or a hand-written payload. Fix: refuse a `committedAt` later than now() plus a small skew, and/or order the stale check by server-side `at`.
findings.scenario: A developer's clock reads 2027, and their push with committedAt 2027-03-01 is applied on main. Every correct push afterwards gets 'stale: … older than …' until March 2027.

findings.message: The read in lastApplied, the apply and the recordPush each run in their own transaction, with no lock on the project and branch. Two pushes running at once can both pass the stale check, and the older commit can then land after the newer one. The guarantee 'never from a commit older than the last one applied' has no two-session test. Fix: take a lock per project and ref (an advisory lock, or `select … for update` on the project) around the check and the apply. Add a test that runs two real sessions.
findings.scenario: Pushes A (09:00) and B (10:00) on main run at once. Both read no row in lastApplied, B applies first, then A applies and overwrites B's titles and task counts.

findings.message: pushRefusal only stops a phase from moving back. The stale check is per branch, so a lagging branch can still overwrite main's newer title, meta (pr, verdict) and tasks_done with older values. That contradicts the comment 'A branch that lags main must not undo what main already moved forward'. Fix: run the staleness check across all branches of the project, or refuse field regressions for each record (tasksDone dropping, pr or verdict being cleared).
findings.scenario: main applies FLT-101 with T2 done and pr set. A push from specclaw/101-export at an older commit (allowed, as the AC-8 test shows) then writes tasks_done back to 1 and sets pr to null.

findings.message: With dryRun false, each record is a separate syncProposal write, and recordPush runs only after all of them succeed. If a record throws anything other than KeyTakenError, the earlier records stay written but no sync_push row is recorded. The Repo sync card then shows nothing, and lastApplied doesn't know about this commit, so the stale guard misses it. Fix: record the push as failed or partial, with its counts, in a finally/catch, or apply everything inside one transaction.
findings.scenario: Out of 50 records, the 30th fails (for example a constraint error). 29 proposals are updated, no sync_push row exists, and an older commit can then push over them.

findings.message: An applied push with only `skipped` entries still writes a sync_push row and an audit event. Archived changes that aren't yet Released always come back as skipped ('released comes from Prod deployments'), so the same unchanged state writes a new row and audit on every push. That contradicts the README's 'A push with nothing new writes nothing'. The AC-7 test passes only because its fixture leaves out the archived change. Fix: write the row only when created or updated is non-zero, or only when the skipped set differs from the last applied one.
findings.scenario: A repo with archived 103-old (not in Prod) pushes the same commit three times with dryRun false. That gives three 'applied 0 created · 0 updated' rows and three audit events.

findings.message: With `--apply`, a run applies nothing if the preview has any skipped lines. An archived change waiting for a Prod deployment, or a branch behind on one proposal, gives a skipped line on every run. So the scheduled routine stops syncing all other changes until a person steps in, and keeps doing so on every run. Fix: let --apply go ahead when the only skips are the documented, expected kinds (Released pending, would move back). Or apply the clean records and report the skips.
findings.scenario: An hourly routine runs on a repo where 101 is archived and not yet deployed. Each run reports one skipped line and applies nothing, so new task ticks on 102 never reach amax.

findings.message: The dry run's `held` query writes out syncProposal's KeyTakenError rule again (services.ts:234). The copies already differ in scope: the dry run filters by project, while syncProposal looks the key up across the whole tenant. A preview can therefore count as created a row that the apply then skips. Fix: share one predicate.

The card pins with the label `CON repo sync`, but get_repo_sync's `of: pinOf.project` returns the project's name. The chip's label changes once chat refreshes it, and the pin resolves to the project instead of the repo-sync view. Fix: give get_repo_sync its own `of` that builds the label from the record, the same way the page does.

pushBy shows every push by a user actor as 'Claude for X'. A person calling sync_specclaw from another MCP client, or directly, is labelled as Claude, which misstates who did it (rule 4). Fix: build the label from the actor and source that were recorded.

`lastApplied` and the card's "Last sync" line are worked out only from the 20 most recent rows. Refused pushes write a row on every run, so they can push the last applied push out of that window. The card then reports that nothing was ever applied. Fix: query the latest applied push separately (as `lastApplied()` already does for the stale gate), and don't infer it from a truncated list.
findings.scenario: An hourly routine on a clone with the wrong origin writes 20 refused rows in a day → `getRepoSync`.`lastApplied` is null → the card says "No specclaw push applied yet" even though main was applied yesterday.
